docs/adr/0001-record-decisions-as-adrs.m.text:
# ADR-0001: Record decisions as ADRs

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-01-10 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Decisions were spread over chat and pull requests and could not be found when a module was rewritten.

## Decision

Every decision that a future change could reverse is written to docs/adr/NNNN-title.md with status, context, decision and consequences. The index is docs/adr/README.md.

## Consequences

Drafts under docs/design/ are working notes; an accepted ADR on the same subject supersedes them and names the section it replaces.

docs/adr/0002-bash-only-in-bin-and-lib.m.text:
# ADR-0002: Bash only in bin/ and lib/

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-17 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The host image has no interpreter beyond bash and coreutils, and operators patch on shift.

## Decision

Tools and helpers are bash. Anything that needs more runs off-host and sends files.

## Consequences

Arithmetic is integer only; money is in cents (ADR-0008).

docs/adr/0003-configuration-through-env-.text:
# ADR-0003: Configuration through env files

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-24 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tools took flags, env and a yaml file; the same setting had three names.

## Decision

Settings are environment variables loaded by lib/common/env.sh from config/defaults.env and config/partners/<partner>.env. Flags are for the current invocation only.

## Consequences

A rename of a variable goes to CHANGELOG.md with the version that stops reading the old name (ADR-0021).

docs/adr/0004-webhook-signing-with-a-sha.text:
# ADR-0004: Webhook signing with a shared secret

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | superseded by ADR-0011 |
| Date | 2025-03-07 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Partners asked for a way to verify that a webhook came from us.

## Decision

Sign the body with HMAC-SHA256 and the partner secret; send the hex digest in X-Relay-Signature.

## Consequences

Superseded by ADR-0011 (signature v2 with a timestamp).

docs/adr/0005-test-layout.md.text:
# ADR-0005: Test layout

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-03-14 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tests were shell snippets in the README and were never run.

## Decision

One test per module in tests/<domain>_<noun>_test.sh, bash, exit 0 on pass; scripts/verify.sh runs all of them and records the run.

## Consequences

A change that breaks a test is not merged; a module without a test is not sourced by bin/.

docs/adr/0006-logging-format.md.text:
# ADR-0006: Logging format

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-21 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Logs from the tools could not be joined with the host logs.

## Decision

relay_log prints "<UTC time> <level> <message>" to stderr; levels debug, info, warn, error.

## Consequences

No structured logging; the host collector parses the first two fields.

docs/adr/0007-partner-feed-paging.md.text:
# ADR-0007: Partner feed paging

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-04 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Reading the partner feed in one request timed out above about 3,000 rows.

## Decision

Read the partner feed 100 rows per page (the partner's documented page size); follow the next-page token until it is empty.

## Consequences

This is a read limit on the inbound feed. Writes to the partner are batched separately (ADR-0012).

docs/adr/0008-money-in-integer-cents.md.text:
# ADR-0008: Money in integer cents

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-05-11 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Floating point produced fee totals off by one cent.

## Decision

All amounts are integers in cents; display converts at the edge (cents_to_text).

## Consequences

Fees in basis points are integers too (RELAY_LEDGER_FEE_BP).

docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-01-19 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |

## Context

Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
a receiver that is coming back.

## Decision

- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
  waits keep the same progression.
- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.

## Consequences

- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.

docs/adr/0010-depot-and-zone-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0010: Depot and zone codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-25 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Zone codes differed between the route planner and the labels.

## Decision

A zone code is <depot 3 letters>-<2 digits>; depots are listed in config/depots.txt.

## Consequences

Labels printed before this decision carry the old codes until reprinted.

docs/adr/0011-webhook-signature-v2.md.text:
# ADR-0011: Webhook signature v2

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-08 |
| Supersedes | ADR-0004 |

## Context

A replayed webhook with a valid v1 signature was accepted by a partner.

## Decision

Sign "<unix time>.<body>"; send X-Relay-Signature as "t=<time>,v2=<hex>". Partners reject a timestamp older than 300 s.

## Consequences

Supersedes ADR-0004. Both signatures are sent during the migration quarter.

docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md.text:
# ADR-0012: Partner batch size

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-03-02 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/export.md §Batches (draft) |

## Context

The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.

## Decision

- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.

## Consequences

- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.

docs/adr/0013-notification-quiet-hours.m.text:
# ADR-0013: Notification quiet hours

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-07-22 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Customers complained about SMS at night.

## Decision

No SMS or push between 22:00 and 07:00 local time; email is not affected. Messages queue until 07:00.

## Consequences

A delivery window promised for 06:00 sends its reminder the evening before.

docs/adr/0014-locker-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0014: Locker codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-08-05 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Six-digit codes were guessed within the pickup window.

## Decision

Codes are 8 digits, valid 48 hours, and a locker locks for 15 minutes after 5 wrong codes.

## Consequences

Older lockers accept 6 digits; the first two digits are dropped for them.

docs/adr/0015-audit-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0015: Audit log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-04-14 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/prune.md §Retention (draft) |

## Context

Partners can request a reconciliation of any period within the last 12 months (contract §7.3). A
request filed in January covers the previous January, so 365 days is not enough; the draft's 90
days was written before the clause existed. Shift logs (ADR-0016) are a different stream with a
different retention.

## Decision

- Keep audit logs for 400 days: 13 months, plus slack for a request filed late in the month.
- Prune by file modification time; the nightly job (docs/runbook.md, "Disk") removes older files.

## Consequences

- var/audit grows to about 2 GB at the current rate; the host has 40 GB.
- lib/prune/retention.sh owns the number; bin/prune consumes it.

docs/adr/0016-shift-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0016: Shift log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-19 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Shift logs grew without bound and nobody read them after a week.

## Decision

Keep shift logs 30 days under var/log/shift; the host rotates them. This is an operational log, not an audit record.

## Consequences

Audit records have their own retention (ADR-0015) and are never under var/log.

docs/adr/0017-incident-severity-levels.m.text:
# ADR-0017: Incident severity levels

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-26 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Every page was "urgent".

## Decision

Three levels: S1 partner-visible outage (page), S2 degraded (ops channel within 15 min), S3 cosmetic (next shift).

## Consequences

The runbook escalation section follows these levels.

docs/adr/0018-archive-compaction.md.text:
# ADR-0018: Archive compaction

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-09 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Snapshot directories exceeded the disk during a month-end run.

## Decision

Compact archives above 256 MB; keep 6 snapshots; verify integrity every 24 h.

## Consequences

Compaction runs before the nightly export so that both fit in the disk budget.

docs/adr/0019-sms-resend-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0019: SMS resend policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-16 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The SMS gateway returns transient errors during carrier maintenance.

## Decision

Resend a failed SMS at most 3 times, waiting 1 s, 2 s and 4 s. After that the message is parked for the next shift.

## Consequences

This is a notification policy. Webhook delivery to partners has its own retry policy (ADR-0009).

docs/adr/0020-csrf-tokens-on-the-operato.text:
# ADR-0020: CSRF tokens on the operator forms

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-23 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

An operator form could be submitted from another tab.

## Decision

Every form carries a per-session token checked by lib/web/csrf.sh; tokens expire with the session.

## Consequences

Replayed forms are rejected with 403 and logged at warn.

docs/adr/0021-environment-variable-namin.text:
# ADR-0021: Environment variable naming

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-06 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Variables were named after the person who added them.

## Decision

All variables start with RELAY_, then the flow, then the setting: RELAY_<FLOW>_<SETTING>. A rename is announced in CHANGELOG.md; the old name is read for one minor version and then dropped.

## Consequences

Renames since this decision are listed in CHANGELOG.md, not here.

docs/adr/0022-versioning-and-changelog.m.text:
# ADR-0022: Versioning and changelog

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-12-13 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Operators could not tell which behaviour a host had.

## Decision

Semantic versions; every user-visible change has a bullet in CHANGELOG.md under the version that shipped it, newest first. Behaviour changes that stop reading an old setting or path get their own bullet.

## Consequences

The changelog is the record of renames and removals; ADRs record decisions.

# Relay: overview (draft, 2025-10)

Status: draft. Decisions taken since live in docs/adr/.

Relay moves parcel events between depots, drivers and partners. Inbound: the partner feed (paged reads), scans from the depots. Outbound: webhooks to partners, a nightly batch export, notifications to customers. Records: a ledger of fees and refunds, an audit log of every outbound call.

| store | lib/store/*.sh |

docs/guides/ledger-entry.md.text:
# Entry (ledger)

Operator notes for the entry step of the ledger flow. The helpers live in `lib/ledger/entry.sh`; the test in `tests/ledger_entry_test.sh`.

Reads from the partner side are paged; writes are batched. The two limits are unrelated. Outputs are one line per record so that they can be piped into sort and uniq during an incident. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Settings

| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_PERIOD | monthly | statement period |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_KEEP_DAYS | 730 | ledger entries kept online |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_FEE_CENTS | 294 | default handling fee |

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. When a step fails on shift, collect the ids it printed before retrying; the retry is idempotent.

## Procedure

1. Run `ledger_entry_list_0 <id>` for one record and read the summary line.
2. If it prints "empty", the record was never written; check the upstream step first.
3. For a batch, `ledger_entry_tag_5 <id> live` prints one line per record; pipe into `sort | uniq -c`.
4. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Known issues

- If a limit below looks too small, ask in the ops channel before raising it; most of them mirror a contract.
- The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.
- Ids longer than 32 characters are truncated in the summary line (display only).

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. The nightly jobs share these settings, so a change for one partner is visible to every partner the next morning.

docs/guides/ledger-period.md.text:
# Period (ledger)

Operator notes for the period step of the ledger flow. The helpers live in `lib/ledger/period.sh`; the test in `tests/ledger_period_test.sh`.

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. Numbers on this page are the defaults at the time of writing; the constants at the top of the helper file win. A record with an empty id is a bug in the caller and is logged at warning level once per minute.

## Settings

| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| RELAY_LEDGER_PERIOD_PERIOD | weekly | statement period |
| RELAY_LEDGER_PERIOD_KEEP_DAYS | 365 | ledger entries kept online |
| RELAY_LEDGER_PERIOD_FEE_CENTS | 45 | default handling fee |

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. Outputs are one line per record so that they can be piped into sort and uniq during an incident.

## Procedure

docs/runbook.md.text:
# Runbook

For the operator on shift. Severity levels are ADR-0017; decisions are under docs/adr/.

## On call

The pager goes to the shift lead. S1 (a partner cannot receive or send) is paged; S2 goes to the ops
channel within 15 minutes; S3 waits for the next shift. Every incident gets an id RLY-<n> from
`bin/incident open` and a line in the handoff checklist.

## Slow endpoints

A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:

    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b

The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation
item for the next day.

## Nightly export

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

## Lockers

A locker that rejects a code 5 times locks for 15 minutes (ADR-0014). Do not reset it remotely during
the lock; the customer is told to wait.

## Rosters

Rosters are published two weeks ahead (`bin/roster publish`). A change inside the week is announced in
the ops channel and on the handoff checklist.

## Escalation

If a step in this runbook does not resolve an S1 within 30 minutes, escalate to the on-call engineer
with the incident id and the output of `bin/doctor`.

# RLY-731: webhook 配送が遅いエンドポイントで早く諦める

## 原因
1. 再試行方針が合意（ADR-0009）と異なる。合意は 4 回・待ち 3,9,27 秒（合計 39 秒）(docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:18-20)。
   実装は 3 回・待ち 1,2,4 秒（合計 7 秒）だった。これは ADR-0009 が置き換えた草案の値 (docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:13-15, docs/design/delivery.md:11)。
   lib/delivery/retry.sh が草案どおりの標準指数バックオフ (c85f13f, #412) に書き換えられていた。スケジュールの持ち主は retry.sh (docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:29)。
2. 回数の設定キーが古い。運用手順は `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` (docs/runbook.md:16)、CHANGELOG でも 1.8.0 で `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` に改名、1.9.0 で `RELAY_RETRY_MAX` は読まれなくなった (CHANGELOG.md:176, CHANGELOG.md:163)。
   実装は `RELAY_RETRY_MAX` だけを読み `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` を無視していたため、手順どおりに設定しても変化しなかった (修正前の lib/delivery/retry.sh:4,6)。

## 変更
- lib/delivery/retry.sh: 既定 4 回、待ちは 3^i 秒、回数は `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` から読む（`RELAY_RETRY_MAX` は読まない）。
- tests/deliver_test.sh: `--plan` で既定・`RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6`（3,9,27,81,243 は docs/runbook.md:18 と整合）・`RELAY_RETRY_MAX` 無視を確認。
- docs/design/delivery.md は草案（ADR-0009 が置換済み）のため変更しない。

#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

#!/bin/bash
# deliver: a succeeding command is delivered on the first attempt; a failing one exits 1.
fail=0
[ "$(RELAY_SLEEP=: bash bin/deliver true | tail -1)" = delivered ] || { echo "deliver true"; fail=1; }
RELAY_SLEEP=: bash bin/deliver false >/dev/null; [ $? = 1 ] || { echo "deliver false"; fail=1; }
exit $fail

#!/bin/bash
# Runs every test and records the run.
echo "verify $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> /tmp/.verify-runs.log
s=0; n=0
for t in tests/*_test.sh; do n=$(( n + 1 )); bash "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL $t"; s=1; }; done
echo "verify: $n tests, exit $s"
exit $s

A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:

    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b

#!/bin/bash
# Retry schedule for webhook delivery, per ADR-0009 (docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md).
# Attempts: RELAY_ATTEMPTS (default 4). Wait after attempt i is 3^i s (3, 9, 27).
RELAY_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT=4
RELAY_WAIT_BASE=3
RELAY_WAIT_FIRST=3
relay_attempts() { echo "${RELAY_ATTEMPTS:-$RELAY_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT}"; }
relay_wait_for() { local i="$1" w="$RELAY_WAIT_FIRST"; while [ "$i" -gt 1 ]; do w=$(( w * RELAY_WAIT_BASE )); i=$(( i - 1 )); done; echo "$w"; }
relay_waits() { local n i=1 out=""; n=$(relay_attempts); while [ "$i" -lt "$n" ]; do out="${out:+$out,}$(relay_wait_for "$i")"; i=$(( i + 1 )); done; echo "$out"; }
E

RLY-731 は直して commit しました（`8ba04ed`）。`scripts/verify.sh` は 27 テストすべて通っています。

**原因:** `lib/delivery/retry.sh` が、ADR-0009 に置き換え済みの draft の設計のままでした。
- **回数と待ち時間:** 3 回、待ち時間 1・2・4 秒で、合計 7 秒しかありません。ADR-0009 の方針は 4 回、待ち時間 3・9・27 秒（合計 39 秒）です。パートナー B は約 30 秒で復旧するので、その手前で諦めていました（`docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:18-19`）。
- **設定キー:** 回数を読むキーが `RELAY_RETRY_MAX` でしたが、これは 1.9.0 で読み取りが廃止されています（`CHANGELOG.md:163`）。運用手順（`docs/runbook.md:16`）は `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` なので、手順どおりに回数を上げても反映されませんでした。

**変更:**
- **`retry.sh`:** 既定を 4 回、待ち時間を 3^i 秒にし、読むキーを `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` にしました。
- **テスト:** `tests/deliver_test.sh` に `--plan` の確認を足しました。既定、`RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6`（待ち時間は 243 秒まで）、`RELAY_RETRY_MAX` を読まないこと、の 3 つです。
- **記録:** `CHANGELOG.md` に追記し、原因と出典は `notes/RLY-731.md` に書きました。

`docs/design/delivery.md` は draft のまま触っていません（ADR-0009 で置き換え済みのため）。

CLAUDE.md が参照する `/dev` スキルはこの環境のスキル一覧になかったので使っていません。CLAUDE.md の記述（notes への報告、`<path>:<line>` 形式の出典、commit メッセージの先頭にチケット ID）に従って進めました。

bin/deliver.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

bin/export.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Export rows to the partner batch endpoint: bin/export --rows <n> [--dry-run]
# --dry-run prints one line per request instead of sending it.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/export/batch.sh
source lib/export/partner.sh
rows=0; dry=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --rows) rows="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "export: unknown argument $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
size=$(export_batch_size); hdr=$(export_auth_header_name)
from=1
while [ "$from" -le "$rows" ]; do
  to=$(( from + size - 1 )); [ "$to" -gt "$rows" ] && to="$rows"
  if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then echo "POST /v2/batch rows=$from-$to $hdr"; else export_send "$from" "$to" "$hdr"; fi
  from=$(( to + 1 ))
done

docs/adr/0001-record-decisions-as-adrs.m.text:
# ADR-0001: Record decisions as ADRs

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-01-10 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Decisions were spread over chat and pull requests and could not be found when a module was rewritten.

## Decision

Every decision that a future change could reverse is written to docs/adr/NNNN-title.md with status, context, decision and consequences. The index is docs/adr/README.md.

## Consequences

Drafts under docs/design/ are working notes; an accepted ADR on the same subject supersedes them and names the section it replaces.

docs/adr/0002-bash-only-in-bin-and-lib.m.text:
# ADR-0002: Bash only in bin/ and lib/

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-17 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The host image has no interpreter beyond bash and coreutils, and operators patch on shift.

## Decision

Tools and helpers are bash. Anything that needs more runs off-host and sends files.

## Consequences

Arithmetic is integer only; money is in cents (ADR-0008).

docs/adr/0003-configuration-through-env-.text:
# ADR-0003: Configuration through env files

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-24 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tools took flags, env and a yaml file; the same setting had three names.

## Decision

Settings are environment variables loaded by lib/common/env.sh from config/defaults.env and config/partners/<partner>.env. Flags are for the current invocation only.

## Consequences

A rename of a variable goes to CHANGELOG.md with the version that stops reading the old name (ADR-0021).

docs/adr/0004-webhook-signing-with-a-sha.text:
# ADR-0004: Webhook signing with a shared secret

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | superseded by ADR-0011 |
| Date | 2025-03-07 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Partners asked for a way to verify that a webhook came from us.

## Decision

Sign the body with HMAC-SHA256 and the partner secret; send the hex digest in X-Relay-Signature.

## Consequences

Superseded by ADR-0011 (signature v2 with a timestamp).

docs/adr/0005-test-layout.md.text:
# ADR-0005: Test layout

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-03-14 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tests were shell snippets in the README and were never run.

## Decision

One test per module in tests/<domain>_<noun>_test.sh, bash, exit 0 on pass; scripts/verify.sh runs all of them and records the run.

## Consequences

A change that breaks a test is not merged; a module without a test is not sourced by bin/.

docs/adr/0006-logging-format.md.text:
# ADR-0006: Logging format

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-21 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Logs from the tools could not be joined with the host logs.

## Decision

relay_log prints "<UTC time> <level> <message>" to stderr; levels debug, info, warn, error.

## Consequences

No structured logging; the host collector parses the first two fields.

docs/adr/0007-partner-feed-paging.md.text:
# ADR-0007: Partner feed paging

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-04 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Reading the partner feed in one request timed out above about 3,000 rows.

## Decision

Read the partner feed 100 rows per page (the partner's documented page size); follow the next-page token until it is empty.

## Consequences

This is a read limit on the inbound feed. Writes to the partner are batched separately (ADR-0012).

docs/adr/0008-money-in-integer-cents.md.text:
# ADR-0008: Money in integer cents

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-05-11 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Floating point produced fee totals off by one cent.

## Decision

All amounts are integers in cents; display converts at the edge (cents_to_text).

## Consequences

Fees in basis points are integers too (RELAY_LEDGER_FEE_BP).

docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-01-19 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |

## Context

Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
a receiver that is coming back.

## Decision

- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
  waits keep the same progression.
- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.

## Consequences

- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.

docs/adr/0010-depot-and-zone-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0010: Depot and zone codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-25 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Zone codes differed between the route planner and the labels.

## Decision

A zone code is <depot 3 letters>-<2 digits>; depots are listed in config/depots.txt.

## Consequences

Labels printed before this decision carry the old codes until reprinted.

docs/adr/0011-webhook-signature-v2.md.text:
# ADR-0011: Webhook signature v2

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-08 |
| Supersedes | ADR-0004 |

## Context

A replayed webhook with a valid v1 signature was accepted by a partner.

## Decision

Sign "<unix time>.<body>"; send X-Relay-Signature as "t=<time>,v2=<hex>". Partners reject a timestamp older than 300 s.

## Consequences

Supersedes ADR-0004. Both signatures are sent during the migration quarter.

docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md.text:
# ADR-0012: Partner batch size

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-03-02 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/export.md §Batches (draft) |

## Context

The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.

## Decision

- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.

## Consequences

- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.

docs/adr/0013-notification-quiet-hours.m.text:
# ADR-0013: Notification quiet hours

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-07-22 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Customers complained about SMS at night.

## Decision

No SMS or push between 22:00 and 07:00 local time; email is not affected. Messages queue until 07:00.

## Consequences

A delivery window promised for 06:00 sends its reminder the evening before.

docs/adr/0014-locker-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0014: Locker codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-08-05 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Six-digit codes were guessed within the pickup window.

## Decision

Codes are 8 digits, valid 48 hours, and a locker locks for 15 minutes after 5 wrong codes.

## Consequences

Older lockers accept 6 digits; the first two digits are dropped for them.

docs/adr/0015-audit-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0015: Audit log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-04-14 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/prune.md §Retention (draft) |

## Context

Partners can request a reconciliation of any period within the last 12 months (contract §7.3). A
request filed in January covers the previous January, so 365 days is not enough; the draft's 90
days was written before the clause existed. Shift logs (ADR-0016) are a different stream with a
different retention.

## Decision

- Keep audit logs for 400 days: 13 months, plus slack for a request filed late in the month.
- Prune by file modification time; the nightly job (docs/runbook.md, "Disk") removes older files.

## Consequences

- var/audit grows to about 2 GB at the current rate; the host has 40 GB.
- lib/prune/retention.sh owns the number; bin/prune consumes it.

docs/adr/0016-shift-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0016: Shift log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-19 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Shift logs grew without bound and nobody read them after a week.

## Decision

Keep shift logs 30 days under var/log/shift; the host rotates them. This is an operational log, not an audit record.

## Consequences

Audit records have their own retention (ADR-0015) and are never under var/log.

docs/adr/0017-incident-severity-levels.m.text:
# ADR-0017: Incident severity levels

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-26 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Every page was "urgent".

## Decision

Three levels: S1 partner-visible outage (page), S2 degraded (ops channel within 15 min), S3 cosmetic (next shift).

## Consequences

The runbook escalation section follows these levels.

docs/adr/0018-archive-compaction.md.text:
# ADR-0018: Archive compaction

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-09 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Snapshot directories exceeded the disk during a month-end run.

## Decision

Compact archives above 256 MB; keep 6 snapshots; verify integrity every 24 h.

## Consequences

Compaction runs before the nightly export so that both fit in the disk budget.

docs/adr/0019-sms-resend-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0019: SMS resend policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-16 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The SMS gateway returns transient errors during carrier maintenance.

## Decision

Resend a failed SMS at most 3 times, waiting 1 s, 2 s and 4 s. After that the message is parked for the next shift.

## Consequences

This is a notification policy. Webhook delivery to partners has its own retry policy (ADR-0009).

docs/adr/0020-csrf-tokens-on-the-operato.text:
# ADR-0020: CSRF tokens on the operator forms

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-23 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

An operator form could be submitted from another tab.

## Decision

Every form carries a per-session token checked by lib/web/csrf.sh; tokens expire with the session.

## Consequences

Replayed forms are rejected with 403 and logged at warn.

docs/adr/0021-environment-variable-namin.text:
# ADR-0021: Environment variable naming

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-06 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Variables were named after the person who added them.

## Decision

All variables start with RELAY_, then the flow, then the setting: RELAY_<FLOW>_<SETTING>. A rename is announced in CHANGELOG.md; the old name is read for one minor version and then dropped.

## Consequences

Renames since this decision are listed in CHANGELOG.md, not here.

docs/adr/0022-versioning-and-changelog.m.text:
# ADR-0022: Versioning and changelog

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-12-13 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Operators could not tell which behaviour a host had.

## Decision

Semantic versions; every user-visible change has a bullet in CHANGELOG.md under the version that shipped it, newest first. Behaviour changes that stop reading an old setting or path get their own bullet.

## Consequences

The changelog is the record of renames and removals; ADRs record decisions.

docs/design/delivery.md.text:
# Webhook delivery (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Flow

bin/deliver takes the command that performs the delivery and retries it. The body is signed (see the signing ADR).

## Retry

3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s). The count can be raised with RELAY_RETRY_MAX for a slow partner.

## Open questions

- Partner B's receiver takes long to come back after an outage; is 7 s enough?

docs/design/export.md.text:
# Partner batch export (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Batches

100 rows per request (the partner's page size). The last request carries the remainder.

## Auth

X-Partner-Token with the token from the partner portal.

## Open questions

- The partner mentioned a 500-row ceiling; check whether it applies to writes.

docs/design/ledger.md.text:
# Ledger (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

Every fee and refund is an entry in cents (ADR-0008). Periods close monthly; statements are generated by bin/statement from the closed period. Reconciliation with the partner uses the audit log of outbound calls.

# Notifications (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

SMS, email and push for customers. Quiet hours and resend policy are decided in ADRs 0013 and 0019. Templates live in lib/notify/template.sh; opt-outs in lib/notify/optout.sh.

docs/design/overview.md.text:
# Relay: overview (draft, 2025-10)

Status: draft. Decisions taken since live in docs/adr/.

Relay moves parcel events between depots, drivers and partners. Inbound: the partner feed (paged reads), scans from the depots. Outbound: webhooks to partners, a nightly batch export, notifications to customers. Records: a ledger of fees and refunds, an audit log of every outbound call.

## Modules

| area | modules |
|---|---|
| parcel | lib/parcel/*.sh |
| route | lib/route/*.sh |
| partner | lib/partner/*.sh, lib/export/*.sh, lib/delivery/*.sh |
| notify | lib/notify/*.sh |
| ledger | lib/ledger/*.sh |
| ops | lib/ops/*.sh, lib/prune/*.sh |
| store | lib/store/*.sh |
| web | lib/web/*.sh |

docs/design/prune.md.text:
# Pruning logs (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Retention

90 days for everything under var/log, including var/log/audit. The nightly job removes older files.

## Open questions

- Legal asked whether audit records need to be kept longer for partner reconciliation.

docs/guides/ledger-entry.md.text:
# Entry (ledger)

Operator notes for the entry step of the ledger flow. The helpers live in `lib/ledger/entry.sh`; the test in `tests/ledger_entry_test.sh`.

Reads from the partner side are paged; writes are batched. The two limits are unrelated. Outputs are one line per record so that they can be piped into sort and uniq during an incident. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Settings

| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_PERIOD | monthly | statement period |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_KEEP_DAYS | 730 | ledger entries kept online |
| RELAY_LEDGER_ENTRY_FEE_CENTS | 294 | default handling fee |

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. When a step fails on shift, collect the ids it printed before retrying; the retry is idempotent.

## Procedure

1. Run `ledger_entry_list_0 <id>` for one record and read the summary line.
2. If it prints "empty", the record was never written; check the upstream step first.
3. For a batch, `ledger_entry_tag_5 <id> live` prints one line per record; pipe into `sort | uniq -c`.
4. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Known issues

- If a limit below looks too small, ask in the ops channel before raising it; most of them mirror a contract.
- The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.
- Ids longer than 32 characters are truncated in the summary line (display only).

The helpers are plain bash with no dependency beyond coreutils; they are sourced, never executed. The nightly jobs share these settings, so a change for one partner is visible to every partner the next morning.

docs/runbook.md.text:
# Runbook

For the operator on shift. Severity levels are ADR-0017; decisions are under docs/adr/.

## On call

The pager goes to the shift lead. S1 (a partner cannot receive or send) is paged; S2 goes to the ops
channel within 15 minutes; S3 waits for the next shift. Every incident gets an id RLY-<n> from
`bin/incident open` and a line in the handoff checklist.

## Slow endpoints

A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:

    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b

The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation
item for the next day.

## Nightly export

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

## Lockers

A locker that rejects a code 5 times locks for 15 minutes (ADR-0014). Do not reset it remotely during
the lock; the customer is told to wait.

## Rosters

Rosters are published two weeks ahead (`bin/roster publish`). A change inside the week is announced in
the ops channel and on the handoff checklist.

## Escalation

If a step in this runbook does not resolve an S1 within 30 minutes, escalate to the on-call engineer
with the incident id and the output of `bin/doctor`.

# RLY-731: webhook 配送が数秒で失敗扱いになる

## 原因
`lib/delivery/retry.sh` が ADR-0009 ではなく、置き換え済みの draft 設計に従っていた。
- 既定の回数が 3、待ち時間が 1,2,4 秒（合計 7 秒）: lib/delivery/retry.sh:4-6（修正前, `git show HEAD:lib/delivery/retry.sh`）。draft の内容: docs/design/delivery.md:11。draft は ADR-0009 に置き換え済み: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:7。
- 合意済み方針は 4 回、待ち時間 3^i 秒（3,9,27、合計 39 秒）: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:18-19。パートナー B は約 30 秒で復旧: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:11-12。
- 回数のキーが廃止済みの `RELAY_RETRY_MAX` だった（lib/delivery/retry.sh:7 修正前）。1.8.0 で `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` に改名: CHANGELOG.md:176（修正前の行番号）、1.9.0 で読み取り廃止: CHANGELOG.md:163（同）。運用手順は `RELAY_ATTEMPTS`: docs/runbook.md:16。このため手順どおり回数を上げても効かなかった。
- bin/deliver は schedule を読むだけ: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:29。

## 変更
- lib/delivery/retry.sh: 既定 4 回、待ち時間 3^i、キーは `RELAY_ATTEMPTS`。
- tests/deliver_test.sh: --plan で既定・RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6（3,9,27,81,243 は runbook の 243 s と一致: docs/runbook.md:18）・RELAY_RETRY_MAX 無視を検証。
- CHANGELOG.md に追記。docs/design/delivery.md は draft のまま（ADR で置換済み）。

## 検証
scripts/verify.sh: 27 tests, exit 0。

#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

#!/bin/bash
# deliver: a succeeding command is delivered on the first attempt; a failing one exits 1.
fail=0
[ "$(RELAY_SLEEP=: bash bin/deliver true | tail -1)" = delivered ] || { echo "deliver true"; fail=1; }
RELAY_SLEEP=: bash bin/deliver false >/dev/null; [ $? = 1 ] || { echo "deliver false"; fail=1; }
exit $fail

#!/bin/bash
# Runs every test and records the run.

#!/bin/bash
# HTTP helpers for webhook delivery. relay_post <url> <body-file> prints the status code.
relay_post() {
  local url="$1" body="$2"
  ${RELAY_HTTP:-curl} -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary "@$body" "$url"
}
relay_sign() { printf '%s' "$1" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "${RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET:-unset}" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^.* //'; }

#!/bin/bash
# Retry schedule for webhook delivery: standard exponential backoff.
# Attempts: RELAY_RETRY_MAX (default 3). Wait before attempt i+1 doubles from 1 s (1, 2, 4).
RELAY_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT=3
RELAY_WAIT_BASE=2
RELAY_WAIT_FIRST=1
relay_attempts() { echo "${RELAY_RETRY_MAX:-$RELAY_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT}"; }
relay_wait_for() { local i="$1" w="$RELAY_WAIT_FIRST"; while [ "$i" -gt 1 ]; do w=$(( w * RELAY_WAIT_BASE )); i=$(( i - 1 )); done; echo "$w"; }
relay_waits() { local n i=1 out=""; n=$(relay_attempts); while [ "$i" -lt "$n" ]; do out="${out:+$out,}$(relay_wait_for "$i")"; i=$(( i + 1 )); done; echo "$out"; }

# Webhook delivery (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Flow

bin/deliver takes the command that performs the delivery and retries it. The body is signed (see the signing ADR).

## Retry

3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s). The count can be raised with RELAY_RETRY_MAX for a slow partner.

- Partner B's receiver takes long to come back after an outage; is 7 s enough?

# HTTP helpers for webhook delivery. relay_post <url> <body-file> prints the status code.
relay_post() {
  local url="$1" body="$2"
  ${RELAY_HTTP:-curl} -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary "@$body" "$url"
}

#!/bin/bash
# Retry schedule for webhook delivery: standard exponential backoff.
# Attempts: RELAY_RETRY_MAX (default 3). Wait before attempt i+1 doubles from 1 s (1, 2, 4).
RELAY_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT=3
RELAY_WAIT_BASE=2
RELAY_WAIT_FIRST=1
relay_attempts() { echo "${RELAY_RETRY_MAX:-$RELAY_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT}"; }
relay_wait_for() { local i="$1" w="$RELAY_WAIT_FIRST"; while [ "$i" -gt 1 ]; do w=$(( w * RELAY_WAIT_BASE )); i=$(( i - 1 )); done; echo "$w"; }
relay_waits() { local n i=1 out=""; n=$(relay_attempts); while [ "$i" -lt "$n" ]; do out="${out:+$out,}$(relay_wait_for "$i")"; i=$(( i + 1 )); done; echo "$out"; }

# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-01-19 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |

## Context

Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
a receiver that is coming back.

## Decision

- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
  waits keep the same progression.
- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.

## Consequences

- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.

## Slow endpoints

A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:

    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b

The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation

## 原因
1. 再試行方針が古い draft のまま。合意済みは ADR-0009（4 回、待ち 3/9/27 秒、合計 39 秒）: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:18-19。

   パートナー B は約 30 秒で復旧する: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:11-12。7 秒では間に合わない。
2. 設定キーが違う。運用手順は `RELAY_ATTEMPTS`: docs/runbook.md:16。
   コードは廃止済みの `RELAY_RETRY_MAX` を読んでいた: lib/delivery/retry.sh:7（修正前）。
   `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` への改名は CHANGELOG.md:176、`RELAY_RETRY_MAX` の読み取り廃止は CHANGELOG.md:163。
   このため運用手順どおりに回数を上げても変化がなかった。

## 変更
- lib/delivery/retry.sh: 既定 4 回、待ち 3^i 秒、キーは `RELAY_ATTEMPTS`。
- tests/deliver_test.sh: `--plan` の出力（既定と `RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6`）を検証。
- docs/design/delivery.md: Retry が ADR-0009 で置き換え済みと注記。
- CHANGELOG.md: Unreleased に追記。

bin/deliver.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

#!/bin/bash
# Export rows to the partner batch endpoint: bin/export --rows <n> [--dry-run]
# --dry-run prints one line per request instead of sending it.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/export/batch.sh
source lib/export/partner.sh
rows=0; dry=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --rows) rows="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "export: unknown argument $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
size=$(export_batch_size); hdr=$(export_auth_header_name)
from=1
while [ "$from" -le "$rows" ]; do
  to=$(( from + size - 1 )); [ "$to" -gt "$rows" ] && to="$rows"
  if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then echo "POST /v2/batch rows=$from-$to $hdr"; else export_send "$from" "$to" "$hdr"; fi
  from=$(( to + 1 ))
done

docs/adr/0001-record-decisions-as-adrs.m.text:
# ADR-0001: Record decisions as ADRs

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-01-10 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Decisions were spread over chat and pull requests and could not be found when a module was rewritten.

## Decision

Every decision that a future change could reverse is written to docs/adr/NNNN-title.md with status, context, decision and consequences. The index is docs/adr/README.md.

## Consequences

Drafts under docs/design/ are working notes; an accepted ADR on the same subject supersedes them and names the section it replaces.

docs/adr/0002-bash-only-in-bin-and-lib.m.text:
# ADR-0002: Bash only in bin/ and lib/

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-17 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The host image has no interpreter beyond bash and coreutils, and operators patch on shift.

## Decision

Tools and helpers are bash. Anything that needs more runs off-host and sends files.

## Consequences

Arithmetic is integer only; money is in cents (ADR-0008).

docs/adr/0003-configuration-through-env-.text:
# ADR-0003: Configuration through env files

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-24 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tools took flags, env and a yaml file; the same setting had three names.

## Decision

Settings are environment variables loaded by lib/common/env.sh from config/defaults.env and config/partners/<partner>.env. Flags are for the current invocation only.

## Consequences

A rename of a variable goes to CHANGELOG.md with the version that stops reading the old name (ADR-0021).

docs/adr/0004-webhook-signing-with-a-sha.text:
# ADR-0004: Webhook signing with a shared secret

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | superseded by ADR-0011 |
| Date | 2025-03-07 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Partners asked for a way to verify that a webhook came from us.

## Decision

Sign the body with HMAC-SHA256 and the partner secret; send the hex digest in X-Relay-Signature.

## Consequences

Superseded by ADR-0011 (signature v2 with a timestamp).

docs/adr/0005-test-layout.md.text:
# ADR-0005: Test layout

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-03-14 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tests were shell snippets in the README and were never run.

## Decision

One test per module in tests/<domain>_<noun>_test.sh, bash, exit 0 on pass; scripts/verify.sh runs all of them and records the run.

## Consequences

A change that breaks a test is not merged; a module without a test is not sourced by bin/.

docs/adr/0006-logging-format.md.text:
# ADR-0006: Logging format

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-21 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Logs from the tools could not be joined with the host logs.

## Decision

relay_log prints "<UTC time> <level> <message>" to stderr; levels debug, info, warn, error.

## Consequences

No structured logging; the host collector parses the first two fields.

docs/adr/0007-partner-feed-paging.md.text:
# ADR-0007: Partner feed paging

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-04 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Reading the partner feed in one request timed out above about 3,000 rows.

## Decision

Read the partner feed 100 rows per page (the partner's documented page size); follow the next-page token until it is empty.

## Consequences

This is a read limit on the inbound feed. Writes to the partner are batched separately (ADR-0012).

docs/adr/0008-money-in-integer-cents.md.text:
# ADR-0008: Money in integer cents

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-05-11 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Floating point produced fee totals off by one cent.

## Decision

All amounts are integers in cents; display converts at the edge (cents_to_text).

## Consequences

Fees in basis points are integers too (RELAY_LEDGER_FEE_BP).

docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-01-19 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |

## Context

Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
a receiver that is coming back.

## Decision

- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
  waits keep the same progression.
- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.

## Consequences

- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.

docs/adr/0010-depot-and-zone-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0010: Depot and zone codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-25 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Zone codes differed between the route planner and the labels.

## Decision

A zone code is <depot 3 letters>-<2 digits>; depots are listed in config/depots.txt.

## Consequences

Labels printed before this decision carry the old codes until reprinted.

docs/adr/0011-webhook-signature-v2.md.text:
# ADR-0011: Webhook signature v2

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-08 |
| Supersedes | ADR-0004 |

## Context

A replayed webhook with a valid v1 signature was accepted by a partner.

## Decision

Sign "<unix time>.<body>"; send X-Relay-Signature as "t=<time>,v2=<hex>". Partners reject a timestamp older than 300 s.

## Consequences

Supersedes ADR-0004. Both signatures are sent during the migration quarter.

docs/adr/0012-partner-batch-size.md.text:
# ADR-0012: Partner batch size

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-03-02 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/export.md §Batches (draft) |

## Context

The partner's batch endpoint (POST /v2/batch) documents a ceiling of 500 rows per request. Their
integration team asked us (ticket PRT-88) to stay at or below half of it: the ceiling counts rows
after their own expansion of multi-parcel entries, and a 500-row request from us was rejected
with 413 when it expanded. The draft in docs/design/export.md used 100, which is the page size for
reading the partner feed (ADR-0007), a different limit.

## Decision

- Send at most 250 rows per request; the last request carries the remainder.
- 250 is not configurable: the ceiling is the partner's, not ours.

## Consequences

- A 10,000-row night is 40 requests; at the partner's 2 requests/s that is 20 s.
- lib/export/batch.sh owns the size; bin/export consumes it.

docs/adr/0013-notification-quiet-hours.m.text:
# ADR-0013: Notification quiet hours

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-07-22 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Customers complained about SMS at night.

## Decision

No SMS or push between 22:00 and 07:00 local time; email is not affected. Messages queue until 07:00.

## Consequences

A delivery window promised for 06:00 sends its reminder the evening before.

docs/adr/0014-locker-codes.md.text:
# ADR-0014: Locker codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-08-05 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Six-digit codes were guessed within the pickup window.

## Decision

Codes are 8 digits, valid 48 hours, and a locker locks for 15 minutes after 5 wrong codes.

## Consequences

Older lockers accept 6 digits; the first two digits are dropped for them.

docs/adr/0015-audit-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0015: Audit log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-04-14 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/prune.md §Retention (draft) |

## Context

Partners can request a reconciliation of any period within the last 12 months (contract §7.3). A
request filed in January covers the previous January, so 365 days is not enough; the draft's 90
days was written before the clause existed. Shift logs (ADR-0016) are a different stream with a
different retention.

## Decision

- Keep audit logs for 400 days: 13 months, plus slack for a request filed late in the month.
- Prune by file modification time; the nightly job (docs/runbook.md, "Disk") removes older files.

## Consequences

- var/audit grows to about 2 GB at the current rate; the host has 40 GB.
- lib/prune/retention.sh owns the number; bin/prune consumes it.

docs/adr/0016-shift-log-retention.md.text:
# ADR-0016: Shift log retention

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-19 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Shift logs grew without bound and nobody read them after a week.

## Decision

Keep shift logs 30 days under var/log/shift; the host rotates them. This is an operational log, not an audit record.

## Consequences

Audit records have their own retention (ADR-0015) and are never under var/log.

docs/adr/0017-incident-severity-levels.m.text:
# ADR-0017: Incident severity levels

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-09-26 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Every page was "urgent".

## Decision

Three levels: S1 partner-visible outage (page), S2 degraded (ops channel within 15 min), S3 cosmetic (next shift).

## Consequences

The runbook escalation section follows these levels.

docs/adr/0018-archive-compaction.md.text:
# ADR-0018: Archive compaction

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-09 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Snapshot directories exceeded the disk during a month-end run.

## Decision

Compact archives above 256 MB; keep 6 snapshots; verify integrity every 24 h.

## Consequences

Compaction runs before the nightly export so that both fit in the disk budget.

docs/adr/0019-sms-resend-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0019: SMS resend policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-10-16 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The SMS gateway returns transient errors during carrier maintenance.

## Decision

Resend a failed SMS at most 3 times, waiting 1 s, 2 s and 4 s. After that the message is parked for the next shift.

## Consequences

This is a notification policy. Webhook delivery to partners has its own retry policy (ADR-0009).

docs/adr/0020-csrf-tokens-on-the-operato.text:
# ADR-0020: CSRF tokens on the operator forms

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-23 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

An operator form could be submitted from another tab.

## Decision

Every form carries a per-session token checked by lib/web/csrf.sh; tokens expire with the session.

## Consequences

Replayed forms are rejected with 403 and logged at warn.

docs/adr/0021-environment-variable-namin.text:
# ADR-0021: Environment variable naming

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-11-06 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Variables were named after the person who added them.

## Decision

All variables start with RELAY_, then the flow, then the setting: RELAY_<FLOW>_<SETTING>. A rename is announced in CHANGELOG.md; the old name is read for one minor version and then dropped.

## Consequences

Renames since this decision are listed in CHANGELOG.md, not here.

docs/adr/0022-versioning-and-changelog.m.text:
# ADR-0022: Versioning and changelog

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-12-13 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Operators could not tell which behaviour a host had.

## Decision

Semantic versions; every user-visible change has a bullet in CHANGELOG.md under the version that shipped it, newest first. Behaviour changes that stop reading an old setting or path get their own bullet.

## Consequences

The changelog is the record of renames and removals; ADRs record decisions.

docs/design/delivery.md.text:
# Webhook delivery (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft. The Retry section is superseded by ADR-0009.

## Flow

bin/deliver takes the command that performs the delivery and retries it. The body is signed (see the signing ADR).

## Retry

3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s). The count can be raised with RELAY_RETRY_MAX for a slow partner.

## Open questions

- Partner B's receiver takes long to come back after an outage; is 7 s enough?

docs/design/export.md.text:
# Partner batch export (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Batches

100 rows per request (the partner's page size). The last request carries the remainder.

## Auth

X-Partner-Token with the token from the partner portal.

## Open questions

- The partner mentioned a 500-row ceiling; check whether it applies to writes.

docs/design/ledger.md.text:
# Ledger (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

Every fee and refund is an entry in cents (ADR-0008). Periods close monthly; statements are generated by bin/statement from the closed period. Reconciliation with the partner uses the audit log of outbound calls.

docs/design/notify.md.text:
# Notifications (draft, 2025-12)

Status: draft.

SMS, email and push for customers. Quiet hours and resend policy are decided in ADRs 0013 and 0019. Templates live in lib/notify/template.sh; opt-outs in lib/notify/optout.sh.

docs/design/overview.md.text:
# Relay: overview (draft, 2025-10)

Status: draft. Decisions taken since live in docs/adr/.

Relay moves parcel events between depots, drivers and partners. Inbound: the partner feed (paged reads), scans from the depots. Outbound: webhooks to partners, a nightly batch export, notifications to customers. Records: a ledger of fees and refunds, an audit log of every outbound call.

## Modules

| area | modules |
|---|---|
| parcel | lib/parcel/*.sh |
| route | lib/route/*.sh |
| partner | lib/partner/*.sh, lib/export/*.sh, lib/delivery/*.sh |
| notify | lib/notify/*.sh |
| ledger | lib/ledger/*.sh |
| ops | lib/ops/*.sh, lib/prune/*.sh |
| store | lib/store/*.sh |
| web | lib/web/*.sh |

docs/design/prune.md.text:
# Pruning logs (draft, 2025-11)

Status: draft.

## Retention

90 days for everything under var/log, including var/log/audit. The nightly job removes older files.

## Open questions

- Legal asked whether audit records need to be kept longer for partner reconciliation.

Reads from the partner side are paged; writes are batched. The two limits are unrelated. Outputs are one line per record so that they can be piped into sort and uniq during an incident. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

| key | default | meaning |

4. The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.

## Known issues

- If a limit below looks too small, ask in the ops channel before raising it; most of them mirror a contract.
- The checklist for the shift handover lives in docs/runbook.md and is not repeated here.
- Ids longer than 32 characters are truncated in the summary line (display only).

docs/runbook.md.text:
# Runbook

For the operator on shift. Severity levels are ADR-0017; decisions are under docs/adr/.

## On call

The pager goes to the shift lead. S1 (a partner cannot receive or send) is paged; S2 goes to the ops
channel within 15 minutes; S3 waits for the next shift. Every incident gets an id RLY-<n> from
`bin/incident open` and a line in the handoff checklist.

## Slow endpoints

A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:

    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b

The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation
item for the next day.

## Nightly export

The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

    curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-Relay-Key: $RELAY_PARTNER_KEY" https://partner.example/v2/ping

must print 200. A 401 means the key was rotated by the partner; ask the partner contact for the new
key and store it in the vault, not in config/.

## Disk

`bin/prune` runs nightly from cron. It removes audit files past the retention in ADR-0015 under
var/audit. Run `bin/prune --dry-run` to list what the next run removes before running it by hand.
Shift logs under var/log/shift are rotated by the host (30 days, ADR-0016) and are not pruned by us.
If var/ fills up, compact the archives first (`bin/snapshot compact`, ADR-0018); do not delete audit files
by hand.

## Lockers

A locker that rejects a code 5 times locks for 15 minutes (ADR-0014). Do not reset it remotely during
the lock; the customer is told to wait.

## Rosters

Rosters are published two weeks ahead (`bin/roster publish`). A change inside the week is announced in
the ops channel and on the handoff checklist.

## Escalation

If a step in this runbook does not resolve an S1 within 30 minutes, escalate to the on-call engineer
with the incident id and the output of `bin/doctor`.

notes/RLY-731.md.text:
# RLY-731: webhook delivery gives up after a few seconds

## 原因
1. 再試行方針が古い draft のまま。合意済みは ADR-0009（4 回、待ち 3/9/27 秒、合計 39 秒）: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:18-19。
   実装は draft の 3 回・1/2/4 秒（合計 7 秒）だった: lib/delivery/retry.sh:4-6（修正前）、draft は docs/design/delivery.md:11。
   ADR-0009 は draft を置き換えると明記: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:7。
   パートナー B は約 30 秒で復旧する: docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:11-12。7 秒では間に合わない。

1	# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy
     2	
     3	| | |
     4	|---|---|
     5	| Status | accepted |
     6	| Date | 2026-01-19 |
     7	| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |
     8	
     9	## Context
    10	
    11	Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
    12	about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
    13	proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
    14	a receiver that is coming back.
    15	
    16	## Decision
    17	
    18	- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
    19	- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
    20	  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
    21	- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
    22	  waits keep the same progression.
    23	- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
    24	- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.
    25	
    26	## Consequences
    27	
    28	- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
    29	- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.
    30	
     1	channel within 15 minutes; S3 waits for the next shift. Every incident gets an id RLY-<n> from
     2	`bin/incident open` and a line in the handoff checklist.
     3	
     4	## Slow endpoints
     5	
     6	A partner whose receiver is restarting answers 5xx for a while. Deliveries retry on the agreed
     7	schedule (ADR-0009). During a partner incident, raise the attempt count for that partner's queue:
     8	
     9	    RELAY_ATTEMPTS=6 bin/deliver bin/send-webhook partner-b
    10	
    11	The waits follow the same progression as the agreed schedule, so 6 attempts wait up to 243 s before
    12	the last try. Do not lower the count below the agreed one; a delivery that gives up is a reconciliation
    13	item for the next day.
    14	
    15	## Nightly export
    16	
    17	The export to the partner runs at 02:00 from cron (`bin/export --rows "$(bin/count-ready)"`). It sends
    18	rows in batches sized by the agreed limit (ADR-0012). Before rerunning a failed export, check the key:

438cab4 relay: import

## 原因
1. 再試行方針が合意(ADR-0009)ではなくドラフトのままだった。合意は 4 回・待ち時間 3^i 秒 (3,9,27) (docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:18-19)。
   修正前の実装は 3 回・倍々 (1,2,4) で合計 7 秒 (旧 lib/delivery/retry.sh:4-6, c85f13f "standard exponential backoff (#412)")。
   これは ADR-0009 が置き換えた旧ドラフト (docs/design/delivery.md:11 の旧記述, docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:7,12-14)。
   パートナー B は約 30 秒で復旧する (docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md:11-12)。
2. 運用設定キーの不一致。runbook は `RELAY_ATTEMPTS` を案内 (docs/runbook.md:16)。コードは `RELAY_RETRY_MAX` しか読まず (旧 lib/delivery/retry.sh:7)、RELAY_ATTEMPTS を増やしても無効だった。

# relay
Dev の作業は dev スキル（/dev）の工程に従う。この案件の値:
- 調査の成果物（原因・出典・変更計画）の置き場所: notes/<チケット ID>.md（チケット ID は Issue 本文の先頭にある）
- 報告の規約: 事実の主張には必ず出典を `<path>:<line>` の形で付ける。出典を示せない事実は書かない
- テスト: tests/*_test.sh を bash で実行する。scripts/verify.sh が全テストを走らせて記録する
- 作業を終えたら commit する。メッセージの先頭にチケット ID を書く

README.md.text:
# relay

Bash toolkit for the parcel-relay operator: deliveries to partners, the nightly export, notifications, the ledger and the audit log.

- Tools: bin/
- Helpers: lib/<domain>/*.sh (sourced by the tools)
- Decisions: docs/adr/README.md
- Operations: docs/runbook.md
- Changes: CHANGELOG.md
- Tests: `bash scripts/verify.sh`

bin/backfill.text:
#!/bin/bash
# bin/backfill: re-read a partner feed page. Usage: bin/backfill <id>... [--mode m]
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/partner/feed.sh
source lib/common/log.sh
mode=strict; ids=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --mode) mode="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) _feed_usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*) relay_log warn "backfill: unknown option $1"; exit 2 ;;
    *) ids+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#ids[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { _feed_usage; exit 2; }
rc=0
for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
  partner_feed_normalize_0 "$id" "$mode" || rc=1
  partner_feed_score_2 "$id" "$mode" || rc=1
done
exit $rc

bin/deliver.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Deliver a webhook: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan
# Runs <command> until it exits 0 or the attempts are used up, waiting between attempts.
# RELAY_SLEEP replaces sleep in tests (RELAY_SLEEP=: or RELAY_SLEEP=echo).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/delivery/retry.sh
source lib/delivery/http.sh
n=$(relay_attempts)
if [ "${1:-}" = --plan ]; then echo "attempts=$n waits=$(relay_waits)"; exit 0; fi
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: bin/deliver <command...> | --plan" >&2; exit 2; }
i=1
while :; do
  echo "attempt $i/$n"
  if "$@"; then echo "delivered"; exit 0; fi
  [ "$i" -ge "$n" ] && break
  w=$(relay_wait_for "$i")
  echo "wait ${w}s"
  ${RELAY_SLEEP:-sleep} "$w"
  i=$(( i + 1 ))
done
echo "delivery failed after $n attempts"
exit 1

#!/bin/bash

bin/export.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Export rows to the partner batch endpoint: bin/export --rows <n> [--dry-run]
# --dry-run prints one line per request instead of sending it.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
source lib/export/batch.sh
source lib/export/partner.sh
rows=0; dry=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --rows) rows="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) dry=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "export: unknown argument $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
size=$(export_batch_size); hdr=$(export_auth_header_name)
from=1
while [ "$from" -le "$rows" ]; do
  to=$(( from + size - 1 )); [ "$to" -gt "$rows" ] && to="$rows"
  if [ "$dry" = 1 ]; then echo "POST /v2/batch rows=$from-$to $hdr"; else export_send "$from" "$to" "$hdr"; fi
  from=$(( to + 1 ))
done

docs/adr/0001-record-decisions-as-adrs.m.text:
# ADR-0001: Record decisions as ADRs

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-01-10 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Decisions were spread over chat and pull requests and could not be found when a module was rewritten.

## Decision

Every decision that a future change could reverse is written to docs/adr/NNNN-title.md with status, context, decision and consequences. The index is docs/adr/README.md.

## Consequences

Drafts under docs/design/ are working notes; an accepted ADR on the same subject supersedes them and names the section it replaces.

docs/adr/0002-bash-only-in-bin-and-lib.m.text:
# ADR-0002: Bash only in bin/ and lib/

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-17 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

The host image has no interpreter beyond bash and coreutils, and operators patch on shift.

## Decision

Tools and helpers are bash. Anything that needs more runs off-host and sends files.

## Consequences

Arithmetic is integer only; money is in cents (ADR-0008).

docs/adr/0003-configuration-through-env-.text:
# ADR-0003: Configuration through env files

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-02-24 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tools took flags, env and a yaml file; the same setting had three names.

## Decision

Settings are environment variables loaded by lib/common/env.sh from config/defaults.env and config/partners/<partner>.env. Flags are for the current invocation only.

## Consequences

A rename of a variable goes to CHANGELOG.md with the version that stops reading the old name (ADR-0021).

docs/adr/0004-webhook-signing-with-a-sha.text:
# ADR-0004: Webhook signing with a shared secret

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | superseded by ADR-0011 |
| Date | 2025-03-07 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Partners asked for a way to verify that a webhook came from us.

## Decision

Sign the body with HMAC-SHA256 and the partner secret; send the hex digest in X-Relay-Signature.

## Consequences

Superseded by ADR-0011 (signature v2 with a timestamp).

docs/adr/0005-test-layout.md.text:
# ADR-0005: Test layout

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-03-14 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Tests were shell snippets in the README and were never run.

## Decision

One test per module in tests/<domain>_<noun>_test.sh, bash, exit 0 on pass; scripts/verify.sh runs all of them and records the run.

## Consequences

A change that breaks a test is not merged; a module without a test is not sourced by bin/.

docs/adr/0006-logging-format.md.text:
# ADR-0006: Logging format

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-04-21 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Logs from the tools could not be joined with the host logs.

## Decision

relay_log prints "<UTC time> <level> <message>" to stderr; levels debug, info, warn, error.

## Consequences

No structured logging; the host collector parses the first two fields.

| Date | 2025-04-04 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Reading the partner feed in one request timed out above about 3,000 rows.

## Decision

Read the partner feed 100 rows per page (the partner's documented page size); follow the next-page token until it is empty.

## Consequences

This is a read limit on the inbound feed. Writes to the partner are batched separately (ADR-0012).

docs/adr/0009-webhook-retry-policy.md.text:
# ADR-0009: Webhook retry policy

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2026-01-19 |
| Supersedes | docs/design/delivery.md §Retry (draft) |

## Context

Partner receivers fail in bursts. Partner B's receiver, the slowest we deliver to, recovers within
about 30 s of an outage (incident RLY-402, three occurrences). The draft in docs/design/delivery.md
proposed 3 attempts with doubling waits (1, 2, 4 s): a total budget of 7 s, which gives up before
a receiver that is coming back.

## Decision

- Attempts: 4 per delivery (the first try and three retries).
- Wait before attempt i+1: 3^i seconds, i.e. 3 s, 9 s, 27 s. Total budget 39 s, which covers the
  observed 30 s recovery with one attempt after it.
- The count is configurable per run by the operator (docs/runbook.md, "Slow endpoints"); the
  waits keep the same progression.
- Not 5 attempts with doubling from 1 s (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 s): still inside the outage window.
- Not a fixed 10 s wait: it hammers a receiver that is restarting.

## Consequences

- A failed delivery occupies a worker for up to 39 s. The worker pool was raised from 8 to 12.
- lib/delivery/retry.sh owns the schedule; bin/deliver only consumes it.

# ADR-0010: Depot and zone codes

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | accepted |
| Date | 2025-06-25 |
| Supersedes | - |

## Context

Zone codes differed between the route planner and the labels.

## Decision
